title: They fought… over a dead man.
paragraphs: They fought… over a dead man.

Not for land.
Not for power.
For a body.
In one of the most mysterious moments in Scripture, the Bible pulls back the curtain just a little—and what we see is not human.

📖 “But even the archangel Michael, when he was disputing with the devil about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous accusation against him, but said, ‘The Lord rebuke you!’” — Jude 1:9
Buried by God Himself (Deuteronomy 34:5–6). No grave marker. No monument. No shrine.

Michael the archangel.
Satan, the accuser.

Some scholars interpret that Satan wanted Moses’ body to become an idol—a relic Israel could worship instead of God. Others believe Satan was accusing Moses, pointing to his past failure (striking the rock, disobedience), claiming he was unworthy of honor.

Satan always weaponizes your past.
Your failure.
Your worst moment.

“Look what you did.”
“You don’t deserve redemption.”
“You belong to me.”

But Michael didn’t argue.
Didn’t debate.
Didn’t defend Moses’ record.
Because victory over accusation is not found in your defense—
And that’s where grace walks in.

You see, Moses had failures. Real ones. Costly ones.
But God still buried him with honor.
God still defended what was His.
God still had the final word.
If Satan can accuse Moses, he will accuse you.
But if God can defend Moses…

Because at the cross, every accusation was answered.
Every sin exposed—then paid for.
Not ignored.
📖 “Who will bring any charge against those whom God has chosen? It is God who justifies.” — Romans 8:33

So when the enemy whispers,
“You’re disqualified,”

When shame says,
“You’re still that person,”
You don’t win by arguing with the enemy.
You stand under the authority of Christ.
Someone out there is still fighting accusations God already silenced.
